subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm scoping out a full module for a hovering vehicle, planning around 150 parts with multiple textures and roughly 5.4x2.2x2.0 dimensions, hovering slightly above ground level.

I'm deciding to have the lowest points of the thruster nacelles touch the floor, and sketching the chassis layout with separate box sections for the cab, bed, and hood. I'm also planning to reuse metal/panelled paints from a kit library while adding custom camo/cyberpunk wear textures, plus decorative textures like a windshield HUD, decals, vent grills, warning stripes, and a hood number.

Working out body colors and dimensions...

I'll finish the hood/nose profile and keep the bed separate from the main body extrude, building it as a floor with side walls, tailgate, and cab-back wall. For the militarized look I'm planning a pintle-mounted gatling gun on the bed, rocket pods on the sides, a roll bar/light bar on the cab roof, armor plates, a bullbar up front, and an antenna.

Now I'm designing the four hover thruster pods at the wheel positions—each one a lathe-generated ducted-fan nacelle with an outer bell shape, an inner fan disc, and a glowing blue downward-facing disc at the bottom rim so the glow is visible from underneath.

I'm connecting each pod to the body with angled strut pylons, sizing them so the pod sits outside the body and overlaps slightly at the bottom, then adding stubby canard fins in place of traditional wheel arches.

Writing lathe outline coordinates...

I'm also adding glowing underskirt strips along the body sides and roughing out a slanted windshield as a thin textured plane running from the upper cabin down to the nose.

Sizing side windows against the roof and beltline, then planning a glass texture with reflection streaks. For the paint, I'm setting up a mottled hull color with a noise-based gradient and a dirt tint fading in near the bottom.

Still writing paint logic...

Now I'm listing out the detail textures I'll need: windshield, side windows, a skull-hex door emblem, hood stripes, warning hazard markings, a thruster fan, headlights/taillights, a neon kanji sign on the bed, a license plate, and a HUD overlay -- roughly eight elements total. I'm placing glowing headlight boxes near the nose and adding a cyan visor-style glow strip across the front for a cyberpunk look.

Adding more vehicle pieces now: a dark bull bar near the nose, a front grille texture plane, hood vents and scoop, and roof details like a magenta/cyan light bar, antenna, roof rail, sensor dome, and searchlight. For the doors I'm adding seam lines, handles, and armor slabs with rivet bolts made from merged spheres, and for the bed I'm building the floor, side walls, tailgate, ammo crates, a gatling turret with a six-barrel cylinder cluster and ammo drum, plus rocket pods made from grids of tubes.

Moving to the rear now: glowing taillight strips, a rear bumper, and twin rear thruster pods with a central cyan-glowing thrust nozzle pair modeled as cones. I'm also adding dark skirt armor between pods, small glowing wing mirrors, spare battery cylinders on the bed, and a neon decal plate reading "HV-07" since rendering actual kanji text isn't feasible with basic shapes.

I'm writing a `merged` helper function that combines many small spheres of a given color into a single mesh for efficiency, aiming for a total part count around 150 as I assemble the full vehicle code.

Working out box geometry helpers and noting that since this is a static model without joints, parts attach directly to the root using position options. I'm defining hazard stripe textures for the bull bar and rear bumper, then plotting out the cab's extruded outline as a polygon in the z-y plane, carefully ordering the vertices to avoid self-intersection.

Now I'm calculating the windshield's slope and normal vector to determine its placement and orientation relative to the cab, then starting to work out the side window dimensions and trapezoid shape based on the cab's width.

Working out the viewer's orientation: looking from +X toward -X with up as Y, the cross product gives the viewer's right direction as -Z, which I need to map correctly against the vehicle's front-facing side.

So front appears on the viewer's left for s=1, and on the right for s=-1. I'm planning a function that draws the side window trapezoid with a flip parameter, handling the mirrored case by wrapping the front-at-left version in a transform.

Applying the same mirroring logic to decals, but keeping text unflipped so it always reads correctly regardless of side -- only directional shapes need the flip, symmetric emblems can stay as is. I'm also checking that textured planes use white as a base color and support a glow effect for neon-style signage, and working out pod placement coordinates so they sit just inside the body width without the pylon showing.

That width calculation was too wide for a realistic vehicle, so I'm shrinking the pod radius and pulling them inward to get a tighter, hover-tech proportioned stance while letting the inner edges overlap the body slightly since the skirt will hide it. For the fan detail, I'm placing a downward-facing textured plane with a cyan glow so it's visible from below, plus adding a second upward-facing plane so looking down into the open pod top also reveals the fan blades.

Now I'm adding a glowing flat disc beneath the fan for the underside light effect, a thin neon torus ring around the pod rim for a magenta accent, and mounting brackets with vertical stabilizer fins for added mechanical detail.

Working out the rear nozzle bell shapes next, defining their lathe profiles and axis orientation...

I'm adding a glow disc facing backward at the rear and sizing the nozzles so overall ship length comes out to 6.0 units. Now I'm sketching the bed/floor geometry as a box beneath the main body.

Still placing bed and body panels...

Now for the Gatling gun mount, I'm thinking a pedestal cylinder on the bed raised high enough so the barrel cluster clears the cab roof, positioning it to fire forward over the cab.

Raising gun center to y 2.35 fixes clearance. I'm now sketching the gatling gun assembly—pedestal, yoke box, housing cylinder, and a ring of six barrel cylinders with a muzzle ring and side-mounted ammo drum—before moving on to designing the rocket pods.

Placing twin rocket pods on the bed rails at x=±0.65, facing forward with recessed tube openings and small glowing warhead tips, then positioning ammo crates nearby in the bed.

Adding a roof light bar with magenta/cyan glow segments, a sensor dome, and twin rear antennas rising to about 3.0 height to balance the gun height. For the front I'm sketching a bull bar with a horizontal beam and vertical risers extending outward.

Still placing grille geometry... now I'm adding hood details—vent scoops, hazard stripes, and a number decal plane oriented flat against the hood surface.

Moving on to the doors, I'm laying out seam lines and an armor plate outline extruded along the depth axis near each door's x-position.

I'm also adding an emblem plane centered on the plate, bolt details merged at the corners, panel lines, and defining a rear bumper box geometry.

Still placing details... taillight glow boxes at the tailgate corners, a license plate plane, and neon underglow strips along the side skirts in cyan and magenta. I'm also laying out the underbody floor pan beneath the bed, running from y 0.6 to 1.1.

Now I'm adding mirrors with glowing stripes, exhaust stacks behind the cab as vertical cylinders with orange glow tops, and setting up the color palette with hex values for hull, armor, dark trim, neon cyan, neon magenta, yellow, and orange accents.

I'm defining the hull paint function using noise and color mixing utilities to create a weathered panel look -- blending base tones, darkening lower edges, brightening top surfaces facing the sun, and adding scratch-like highlights from high-frequency noise.

For armor pieces I'll use the metal preset for the bull bar and panels, and I'm planning decal elements like a hexagonal emblem with contrasting colors plus a crate texture with stenciled "AMMO" text on the bed crates. Now I'm starting to scaffold the actual builder module with its config and helper functions.

Writing box, cylinder, and plane helpers...

Still placing pod details...

Still writing fan blade paths... then moving to gatling barrel orientation, windshield texture with reflection streaks and HUD lines, and side window polygon shapes.

I'm working out the rear tailgate sign placement, computing the viewer's right vector by crossing the look and up directions to orient the plane correctly for a camera positioned behind looking forward.

I'm double-checking vertical positions for the ground glow disc and underglow strips against the pod shell's bottom to make sure nothing clips below the floor, then planning the final build: headlight housings as dark boxes, a vent cutout on the hood, and a roof armor plate positioned near the cab's top.

Now I'm placing a light bar atop the roof with alternating cyan and magenta glowing segments, merging each color group separately so the glow effect applies cleanly, plus a small sensor dome sphere near the roof edge before moving on to mirrors.

Then I'm positioning side mirrors with small arm boxes and glowing mirror panels, adding twin exhaust stacks behind the cab with orange glowing ring tops, and placing the gun pedestal at the rear center before starting the Gatling gun geometry itself.

Still writing turret and barrel code...
